qualities.label: perceptual taste quality
qualities.def: A quality of a material entity that is realised when a human perceiver tastes that entity.

qualities.label: basic taste quality
qualities.def: A perceptual taste quality for which a dedicated class of human taste receptor and a dedicated transduction pathway are established.

qualities.label: sweetness
qualities.def: The basic taste quality typically elicited by sucrose and other sugars, transduced by the TAS1R2 and TAS1R3 receptor pair.

qualities.label: sourness
qualities.def: The basic taste quality typically elicited by citric acid and other acids, transduced by proton-sensitive channels of taste receptor cells.

qualities.label: saltiness
qualities.def: The basic taste quality typically elicited by sodium chloride. The epithelial sodium channel is implicated in its transduction, and is well supported in rodents, but a substantial part of human salt taste is amiloride-insensitive and the channel's role in humans remains contested.

qualities.label: bitterness
qualities.def: The basic taste quality typically elicited by quinine and by many plant alkaloids and glycosides, transduced by the TAS2R receptor family.

qualities.label: umami
qualities.def: The basic taste quality typically elicited by L-glutamate and by certain ribonucleotides, transduced by the TAS1R1 and TAS1R3 receptor pair.

qualities.label: candidate taste quality
qualities.def: A perceptual taste quality that has been proposed as basic but for which receptor or transduction evidence remains contested.

qualities.label: fattiness
qualities.def: The candidate taste quality elicited by non-esterified fatty acids, proposed under the name oleogustus and distinct from the texture of fat.

qualities.label: kokumi
qualities.def: The candidate taste quality described as mouthfulness, continuity and thickness, elicited by certain gamma-glutamyl peptides acting on the calcium-sensing receptor.

qualities.label: metallic taste
qualities.def: The candidate taste quality elicited by certain metal salts and reported as a side effect of some medications.

qualities.label: calcium taste
qualities.def: The candidate taste quality elicited by calcium salts, reported as chalky and somewhat bitter.

qualities.label: starchy taste
qualities.def: The candidate taste quality elicited by oligomeric glucose polymers independently of sweetness.

qualities.label: bitterness subtype
qualities.def: A bitterness distinguished by the chemical class of the compound that elicits it and, where known, by the receptor that detects it.

qualities.label: thiourea bitterness
qualities.def: The bitterness elicited by compounds bearing a thiourea group, notably phenylthiocarbamide and propylthiouracil, detected by TAS2R38.

qualities.label: limonoid bitterness
qualities.def: The bitterness elicited by limonoid triterpenoids, notably limonin, which forms from a tasteless precursor after citrus fruit is juiced.

qualities.label: flavanone bitterness
qualities.def: The bitterness elicited by flavanone glycosides, notably naringin, characteristic of grapefruit and pomelo.

qualities.label: alkaloid bitterness
qualities.def: The bitterness elicited by plant alkaloids such as quinine and caffeine.

qualities.label: amino acid bitterness
qualities.def: The bitterness elicited by hydrophobic amino acids and by peptides rich in them, prominent in protein hydrolysates and aged cheese.

qualities.label: chemesthetic quality
qualities.def: A quality perceived in the mouth through the trigeminal nerve rather than through taste receptor cells, recorded alongside taste by sensory panels.

qualities.label: astringency
qualities.def: The chemesthetic quality of drying, roughening and puckering in the mouth, elicited by tannins and other polyphenols binding salivary proteins.

qualities.label: pungency
qualities.def: The chemesthetic quality of burning or stinging, elicited by capsaicinoids, piperine and allyl isothiocyanate.

qualities.label: cooling sensation
qualities.def: The chemesthetic quality of coolness in the absence of a temperature change, elicited by menthol and related compounds.

qualities.label: tingling sensation
qualities.def: The chemesthetic quality of vibration or numbness, elicited by alkylamides such as sanshool.

qualities.label: carbonation bite
qualities.def: The chemesthetic quality elicited by dissolved carbon dioxide, arising from two distinct routes: conversion of carbon dioxide by carbonic anhydrase 4 on sour-sensing taste cells, and a separate trigeminal contribution.

qualities.label: temporal taste quality
qualities.def: A perceptual taste quality defined by when it appears or how long it persists relative to the stimulus entering the mouth.

qualities.label: taste onset latency
qualities.def: The temporal taste quality of how long after the stimulus enters the mouth a taste is first perceived.

qualities.label: aftertaste
qualities.def: The temporal taste quality of a taste that persists after the stimulus has been swallowed or expectorated.

qualities.label: lingering bitterness
qualities.def: An aftertaste that is bitter in quality.

qualities.label: delayed bitterness
qualities.def: A bitterness that is absent or weak when the stimulus is first tasted and appears or strengthens over subsequent minutes to hours.

qualities.label: taste adaptation
qualities.def: The temporal taste quality of a perceived intensity declining during continued exposure to an unchanging stimulus.

qualities.label: hedonic taste quality
qualities.def: A quality of a stimulus consisting in how much a perceiver likes or dislikes tasting it, as distinct from what they perceive.

qualities.label: palatability
qualities.def: The hedonic taste quality of being pleasant to taste for a given perceiver.

qualities.label: taste aversion
qualities.def: The hedonic taste quality of being unpleasant to taste for a given perceiver, whether innately or through learning.

core.label: HTO editors
core.def: Definition source denoting a term authored by the HTO editors for this release rather than taken from a cited publication.

core.label: tasting event
core.def: A planned process in which a human taster orally samples a stimulus and reports one or more perceived taste qualities.

core.label: taster role
core.def: A role borne by a person in virtue of taking part in a tasting event as the person doing the tasting.

core.label: taste stimulus
core.def: A material entity presented to a taster to be tasted.

core.label: reference tastant
core.def: A taste stimulus consisting of a single chemical compound presented at a stated concentration in order to calibrate or classify a taster.

core.label: taste percept assertion
core.def: An information content entity recording that one taster perceived one perceptual taste quality in one stimulus on one occasion.

core.label: intensity rating
core.def: A scalar measurement datum recording how strong a perceived taste quality was, on a stated scale.

core.label: hedonic rating
core.def: A scalar measurement datum recording how much a taster liked or disliked a stimulus, on a stated scale.

core.label: rating scale
core.def: An information content entity specifying the permitted values and anchors used to record a rating.

core.label: detection threshold datum
core.def: A scalar measurement datum recording the lowest concentration of a tastant at which a taster reliably detects that something differs from the blank.

core.label: recognition threshold datum
core.def: A scalar measurement datum recording the lowest concentration of a tastant at which a taster reliably names the quality correctly.

core.label: taster status
core.def: An organism trait classifying a person by their sensitivity to a reference bitter tastant, conventionally propylthiouracil.

core.label: PROP non-taster
core.def: A taster status in which the person reports no bitterness from a propylthiouracil test strip.

core.label: PROP medium taster
core.def: A taster status in which the person reports moderate bitterness from a propylthiouracil test strip.

core.label: PROP super-taster
core.def: A taster status in which the person reports intense bitterness from a propylthiouracil test strip.

core.label: TAS2R38 diplotype
core.def: An information content entity recording the pair of TAS2R38 haplotypes carried by a person, each haplotype being the combination of the amino acid states at positions 49, 262 and 296.

core.label: taste genotype assertion
core.def: An information content entity recording an assertion about a person's genotype at a locus relevant to taste perception.

core.label: tasting session
core.def: A planned process comprising the tasting events performed by one or more tasters on one occasion under one protocol.

core.label: palate cleansing process
core.def: A process performed between tasting events in order to reduce carry-over of taste from the previous stimulus.

core.label: blinding condition
core.def: An information content entity stating what the taster was able to know about the identity of the stimulus at the time of tasting.

core.label: time-intensity profile datum
core.def: A scalar measurement datum recording perceived intensity as a function of time since the stimulus entered the mouth.

core.label: taste confounder
core.def: An information content entity recording a property of a taster that is known to alter taste perception and that should be accounted for when analysing their ratings.

core.label: tobacco use confounder
core.def: A taste confounder recording that the taster currently uses tobacco.

core.label: recent upper respiratory infection confounder
core.def: A taste confounder recording that the taster recently had an upper respiratory infection, including a recent loss of smell.

core.label: xerostomia confounder
core.def: A taste confounder recording that the taster has reduced salivary flow.

core.label: dysgeusia-associated medication confounder
core.def: A taste confounder recording that the taster takes a medication with a documented taste-distortion side effect.

core.label: rating
core.def: A scalar measurement datum recording a value a taster reported on a stated scale, whether of a perceived quality's intensity or of liking.

props.label: has taster
props.def: Relates a tasting event to the person who performed the tasting.

props.label: has stimulus
props.def: Relates a tasting event to the material that was tasted.

props.label: asserts quality
props.def: Relates a taste percept assertion to the perceptual taste quality it reports.

props.label: has intensity rating
props.def: Relates a taste percept assertion to the intensity value reported for it.

props.label: on scale
props.def: Relates a rating to the scale on which it was recorded.

props.label: has hedonic rating
props.def: Relates a tasting event to the liking score the taster gave the sample.

props.label: part of session
props.def: Relates a tasting event to the session in which it took place.

props.label: has taster status
props.def: Relates a person to their assessed taster status.

props.label: has genotype assertion
props.def: Relates a person to a recorded assertion about their taste-related genotype.

props.label: stimulus derived from
props.def: Relates a taste stimulus to the food or beverage class it was prepared from.

props.label: stimulus contains tastant
props.def: Relates a taste stimulus to a chemical entity present in it that bears a taste quality.

props.label: perceived via
props.def: Relates a perceptual taste quality to the biological process by which it is perceived.

props.label: detected by receptor
props.def: Relates a perceptual taste quality to a receptor whose activation is established to contribute to perceiving it.

props.label: has output assertion
props.def: Relates a tasting event to a taste percept assertion produced in it.

props.label: typically associated with diplotype
props.def: Relates a taster status to a diplotype that commonly but not invariably produces it. This is a statistical association and deliberately not an equivalence.

props.label: has diplotype
props.def: Relates a person or a study group to the diplotype they carry, or that characterises them.

props.label: threshold for quality
props.def: Relates a threshold datum to the perceptual taste quality whose detection or recognition it measures.

props.label: rating value
props.def: The numeric value of a rating on its stated scale.

props.label: scale minimum
props.def: The lowest value the scale admits.

props.label: scale maximum
props.def: The highest value the scale admits.

props.label: sample order
props.def: The position of this sample in the order presented to the taster, counting from one.

props.label: is blinded
props.def: True when the taster could not identify the sample at the time of tasting.

props.label: collection date
props.def: The date on which a tasting session was held.

props.label: minutes since preparation
props.def: Minutes elapsed between preparing the stimulus and tasting it. Relevant where a quality develops after preparation, as limonoid bitterness does in citrus juice.

PATO.why: physical object quality, parent of HTO qualities
bitter, the only existing basic taste quality

OBA.why: taste sensitivity trait, parent of taster status

published.population: adults in Japan, PROP taste testing cohort (Aoki et al. 2023, Nutrients 15(10):2415)
published.note: Aoki et al. 2023, doi:10.3390/nu15102415, PMC10222862 (open access; full text fetched and read via eutils efetch db=pmc). Table 2 reports n=24 for PAV/PAV among the 79 subjects who completed PROP taste detection testing by the modified 2AFC procedure with the QUEST method. Section 3.2 (Results) reports the TAS2R38 genotype effect on threshold was significant (one-way ANOVA F(2,76)=163.32, MSE=12.940, p<0.001) and that PAV/PAV differed significantly from AVI/AVI (p<0.001) and from PAV/AVI (p<0.01), but no numeric per-genotype mean/median threshold (in mM or otherwise) is stated anywhere in the article text or its two tables (Table 1: SNP/genotype frequencies; Table 2: demographics only). The only per-genotype threshold values in the paper are shown graphically, on a log scale, in Figure 3 (scatter plot) and Figure 4 (boxplot); those images could not be fetched from this environment (network access is restricted to eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov; www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov and mdpi.com all refused or redirected). Left threshold_mmol_per_l empty rather than estimate a number from an unreadable log-scale figure. The paper does report, in Section 4 Discussion, that AVI/AVI non-tasters separate from other genotypes at approximately 0.3-0.6 mM (a separation boundary, not a per-group mean) and that PAV/PAV and PAV/AVI are on average tens to fifty times more sensitive than AVI/AVI; the QUEST procedure tested concentrations from 0.002 to 3.2 mM (=mmol/L) in 20 log-spaced steps.
